requirements.text: Change the background into a basketball court

outcomes.description: Replace the image background with a basketball court.
outcomes.target: The background is visibly a basketball court, with recognizable court features such as a playing surface and court markings or basketball equipment.
outcomes.reference: The input image and the requested background change in R1.

nodes.question: Compared with the source background, does the edited background now depict a recognizable basketball playing area, rather than basketball equipment against a generic backdrop?
nodes.criteria: Pass when the edited background replaces the source scene with a coherent playing area recognizable as a basketball court, supported by the surface and contextual court features. Fail when the background has changed to basketball-related imagery but remains a generic backdrop with isolated equipment or only an isolated floor line; also fail if no requested background change is visible. Unknown only when the relevant source-to-edit background evidence cannot be assessed.
nodes.binding: Compare the source and edited backgrounds directly; disregard the unchanged foreground person. Judge the background scene as a whole. A hoop or balls alone, or a single line on a floor strip, do not establish a recognizable court. Do not require a regulation layout or prominent markings if the scene otherwise clearly reads as a court.

nodes.question: What visible evidence in the edited background shows that the source background was replaced by a basketball-court playing area, rather than merely adding basketball props?
nodes.criteria: Pass only when the source-to-edit comparison shows a changed background and the edited scene has coherent playing-surface/court context; cite the visible spatial relationship of surface, markings, and basketball context. Fail when the background change is limited to props or generic floor/isolated lines without recognizable court context, or when no requested change is visible. Unknown only if the comparison or relevant background is unassessable.
nodes.binding: Inspect both images and assess the background, not the foreground subject. Do not infer court context from equipment alone or treat a curved line by itself as a court marking. Record concrete visible cues and their relation to the playing surface.

nodes.question: Does the image show the background changed into a recognizable basketball court?
nodes.criteria: Complete if the saved support evidence establishes both that the source background was replaced and that the edited background as a whole is recognizable as a basketball-court playing area. Basketball props, a floor strip, or an isolated line without coherent court context are not sufficient for completion. Partial if evidence establishes basketball-related background progress but not a recognizable court. Absent only if evidence establishes no requested background progress. Unknown if the source-to-edit change or court recognizability remains genuinely unresolved; do not resolve conflicting reports by privileging either one, and do not infer visual facts absent from the supports.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.
